authority: Specification for a separately implemented and independently reviewed primary gate. It does not alter guest.py verdicts.
common_inputs: Pinned suite and helper contents and both candidate hashes; authenticated VM/evaluator identity including root evaluator marker/product UUID equality; case id and mode; complete raw candidate.json including setup, status, error and diagnostics; underlying stdout/stderr/status bytes and all stage records.
capture_rules: Validate each diagnostic capture envelope independently: required stage files must be regular, present, error-free, untruncated, correctly base64 encoded, and captured_bytes must equal the decoded length. Structured control, event, status and assertion records must parse and be internally consistent. Missing, truncated or malformed capture envelopes or malformed control records are infrastructure incomplete. Require files conditionally by stage; retain partial files and setup process output on failure. The namespace event is expected before guard-enter; if namespace setup fails retain any events.jsonl and prepare.log that exist without requiring subsequent files.

candidate.out, candidate.err, baseline.out and baseline.err are arbitrary raw product bytes: never classify them as incomplete merely because their contents are malformed, noncanonical, duplicate, out of range, oversized for the bounded oracle, or unexpected. Once their capture envelopes and invocation controls are complete, classify those semantics as reached product failures.

Do not accept generic harness PASS as evidence without this gate; do not turn generic FAIL into product failure until fixture capability, invocation identity, signal and process scope guards and observation preconditions are established.

setup: If setup fails or times out, classify infrastructure incomplete; preserve setup process stdout/stderr/status and setup.json if present, including partial stage and error. For successful setup require setup.json, stage complete, complete true, parser positive=3 negative=9 ok, compile status 0, guard_control status 0 with exactly one blocked record for each x86_64 syscall number 62, 200, 234, 129, 297, 424, each with SIGSYS 31 and empty stderr, guard_exec status 0 and empty stdout/stderr; validate all base64 fields. Require scope_control status 0, empty stderr, the six EACCES denial lines and allowed caller-stat fixture-directory line exactly; this runs in a separate controlled child. Require namespace_control status 0 and empty stderr, with a parseable namespace-ok record proving a distinct PID namespace, PID=1, parent=0, visible PIDs [1], matching proc self stat, and uid/euid 2000 in the helper.
guard_and_prepare: Require guard-enter PID, ulimit-ok, prepare-ok, fixture.json, oracle.json, prepare.log and completed native controls. Validate PID and SID through recorded real stat, uid-owned fixture root and explicit role bytes. For each observation require scope-start/scope-ok before its recheck, and exactly the matching seven-line native probe record per observation; missing or failed scope control is infrastructure incomplete. Native guard rejects procfs mounts outside /proc, limits Landlock read access to the fixture and explicit runtime paths and the caller's stat, blocks mount, namespace changes, ptrace and process_vm_readv, and closes inherited nonstandard fds. The PID namespace makes even metadata-only PID probing limited to owned processes; the Landlock layer independently denies procfs directory reads and noncaller stat reads.
observation: Validate capture envelopes and structured records separately from raw product bytes. Before each invocation require its successful scope probe, successful recheck of PID and real SID, and ordered start/end events; require complete raw stdout, stderr and status with matching end-event status. Independently parse the raw PID output and compare membership, status and stderr with the role oracle. Complete noncanonical, duplicate, out-of-range or otherwise unexpected output is a product failure, not capture incompleteness. A genuine baseline product failure remains a reached failure even if a later recheck or assertion step is incomplete. When verify completes require parseable assertions and agreement with independent semantic results; contradictory assertions are an infrastructure inconsistency, not a way to erase a separately established product failure. None and unreadable require baseline then target in the same shell and fixture, each independently rechecked.
race: For race, require writer start and completion, race.status 0, empty race.err, complete race.json with reader_open=true and cmdline_removed=true and a complete full stat write, and candidate observation reached. A missing reader, FIFO/control failure, timeout, or incomplete race record is incomplete infrastructure, not a candidate failure. Check bytes_written equals the decoded stat payload length and the payload encodes GONE and outside_sid.
assessment: Classify each completed, independently controlled observation from its own complete raw data; a baseline selected-set, status or stderr mismatch is a reached candidate failure, even if a later target recheck or other infrastructure step fails. Preserve both the baseline product result and later incomplete stage. No case may pass if any required observation or evidence is incomplete. For each fully observed target, classify raw selected-set, status or stderr mismatch as reached candidate failure. Missing, inconsistent or truncated evidence, setup, guard, recheck, writer or assertion infrastructure failure is incomplete. Preserve SIGSYS termination after invocation start for primary review; do not turn incomplete raw evidence into a pass.
unreadable: Require nonempty baseline with its own scope/recheck/complete raw files before seal. Require seal-start, seal-ok, a structured seal record showing caller PID, owner uid 2000, mode 0 and EACCES=13; immediately before target require matching target recheck with mode 0 and EACCES=13. After complete target capture, require status 1, empty stdout and a diagnostic containing the exact bytes opendir /tmp/parity-case/proc-fixture: Permission denied; unrelated opendir errors are product failures. The generic runner's labels are not the gate.
namespace: Before guard-enter require a namespace-ok event from the candidate namespace init control with outer/inner namespace identifiers distinct, parent 1, visible PIDs exactly [1, control PID], matching local proc self stat, and verified uid/euid 2000. Require namespace identity evidence from the root evaluator and native setup; the same freshly mounted private procfs and PID namespace must persist across both baseline and target. The init and candidate and their transient children are owned by the case. If user namespace, mapping, mount or PID/proc isolation is absent or inconsistent, classify infrastructure incomplete. The PID visible to the candidate is used for self and live SID checks. The control outer identifier must match the root evaluator PID namespace; fixture.pid_namespace and every successful observation recheck must match the recorded inner namespace and the caller PID namespace readlink.

always_after_setup_started: setup.json if created; setup process stdout/stderr/status always
after_namespace_started: events.jsonl and prepare.log if created; outer candidate stdout/stderr/status always

limits: The native guard blocks signal syscalls but is not a syscall trace; a killed process may lack its completion record.
A FIFO writer performs a controlled deletion during the stat read; behavior under arbitrary timing or other errors is not established.
A primary gate implementation and review, both guest runs, and adjudication are still required.
PID and procfs isolation depend on guest support for unprivileged user, mount and PID namespaces and a fresh proc mount; unsupported capability is incomplete infrastructure, not a product result.
